correctness.rationale: For −1≤m<0 the proper quadratic −mx²+y²+z² has derivative 2mx²−2nz². Its zero-dissipation set has no invariant orbit except the origin. For m=0, y²+z² controls y,z and the stable linear equation x'=y−x bounds x. A bounded complete omega-limit orbit in {z=0} obeys xy=0; any interval with y≠0 contradicts x'=y−x, and then x'=−x excludes any nonzero bounded complete orbit. The pair of nonzero equilibria for m>0 disproves universal attraction there. At criticality the stable plane is {y=0}. On the center manifold x=h(y), z=k(y), coefficient matching gives h(y)=y+y³/n+(5n+2)y⁵/n³+O(y⁷), k(y)=y²/n+(n+2)y⁴/n³+O(y⁶); the required finite differentiability is available for each fixed n>0. The reduced flow is y'=−a y³−b y⁵+O(y⁷), a=1/n, b=2(n+1)/n³. Thus w=y^(−2) obeys w'=2a+2b/w+O(w^(−2)); first w~2at, then w=2at+O(log t), after which the remainder in w'−2a−(b/a)/t is O(log t/t²) and integrable. The linear stable rates 1,n give exponential tracking in a sufficiently small neighborhood; alternatively, x−h(y), z−k(y) obey a linear stable system up to coefficients tending to zero and decay exponentially, and the small Lipschitz constant of the center flow gives an exponential shadow by solving the scalar error equation backwards from zero error at infinity in an exponential norm. The zero shadow gives the local strong-stable manifold, whose backwards-flow extensions form the global immersed set. For the other shadows the amplitude is of order t^(−1/2) with fixed sign; the exponentially small tracking error changes its reciprocal square by o(1) and does not change the leading limits of x,y,z. The original RESULT.md line 14 has coefficient b/a=2/n+2/n²; it does not have the extra factor shown in the abbreviated frozen-tool display.
residual_risks: Replay verifies the Taylor jet and logarithmic coefficient only. The convergence and tracking conclusions rest on the analytic argument, not numerical integration.
The asymptotics are for fixed n>0 and not uniform as n tends to zero.
